turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Hi, good morning. I'm calling about a valve from Welsford. I need a 2-inch stainless steel ball valve for a water line.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: I don't actually have a part number. I was hoping you could help me figure out which one I need.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: I can't really guess for you. If you don't have the part number, just check the website.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Okay. Do you at least know if the 2-inch stainless one is in stock?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Probably. I'd have to go look. Hold on.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: Sure, I can wait. And while you're checking, how much is it and how fast can you ship it?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: It's whatever the site says, and shipping takes however long it takes. I don't control that.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: All right. Can I just place the order with you over the phone?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You can, but honestly, it's faster if you just do it online yourself. Is there anything else? I've got other calls waiting.

turns.speaker: customer
turns.text: No. No, I guess that's it.

scores.label: Empathy
scores.rationale: No acknowledgment of the customer's situation at any point. Responses are curt and dismissive rather than helpful, and the agent implies impatience instead of reassurance.

evidence.quote: I can't really guess for you.

scores.label: Communication
scores.rationale: Answers are understandable but minimal and non-committal — no explanation, no next steps offered, nothing confirmed in concrete terms.

evidence.quote: It's whatever the site says, and shipping takes however long it takes. I don't control that.

scores.label: Professionalism
scores.rationale: Not overtly hostile, but repeatedly blunt to the point of sounding annoyed, and steers the customer away from doing business over the phone.

evidence.quote: You can, but honestly, it's faster if you just do it online yourself.

scores.label: Process Adherence
scores.rationale: No attempt to look up the part from the description given (size, material, application). Stock was guessed at ('probably') rather than confirmed before answering.

evidence.quote: Probably. I'd have to go look.

scores.label: Issue Resolution
scores.rationale: Call ends with no part identified, no confirmed stock, no price, no shipping estimate, and no order placed — every question the customer asked was deflected.

evidence.quote: Can I just place the order with you over the phone?
No. No, I guess that's it.

strengths.title: Stayed on the call
strengths.detail: Despite the customer not having a part number, the agent kept responding to each question rather than cutting the call short.

strengths.title: Didn't invent an answer
strengths.detail: The agent avoided guessing at exact stock or price rather than telling the customer something that might be wrong.

improvements.title: Offer to look up the part instead of sending the customer away
improvements.detail: "2-inch stainless ball valve for a water line" is enough to search a catalog. Redirecting the customer to do that work themselves loses the sale and the relationship.
improvements.instead: I can't really guess for you. If you don't have the part number, just check the website.
improvements.say: No problem — let me pull up 2-inch stainless ball valves for water line service and we'll find the right one together.

improvements.title: Confirm stock, price, and shipping before answering
improvements.detail: Saying "probably" and "whatever the site says" gives the customer nothing to act on and makes the company look disorganized.
improvements.instead: It's whatever the site says, and shipping takes however long it takes. I don't control that.
improvements.say: Let me check right now — I can give you the exact price and ship date before we hang up.

improvements.title: Don't discourage the customer from buying on the call
improvements.detail: Telling a ready buyer it's "faster" to order online themselves, right after mentioning other calls waiting, reads as wanting to get off the phone rather than close the sale.
improvements.instead: You can, but honestly, it's faster if you just do it online yourself. Is there anything else? I've got other calls waiting.
improvements.say: Absolutely, I can place that order for you right now — let's get it done.

analysis.practiceAction: Before your next call, practice this response for when a customer doesn't have a part number: offer to look it up with them using what they describe, instead of sending them to find it themselves.
flags: no price or shipping info given
customer discouraged from ordering by phone
